content: The following is a detailed guide for creating a WikiDoc Journal Landmark Trial page. A trial page is a comprehensive collection of all the information related to a specific clinical study, including a detailed breakdown of its components. Each study is structured based on various CONSORT checklist items, such as trial design, interventions, outcomes, randomization, statistical methods, and limitations. The templates provided include standardized language to assist in the creation and editing of these pages. Before beginning, it is essential to familiarize yourself with the formatting basics. Below is a checklist of the sections to include when creating your page: Complete Title of Study This section should provide the full title of the study. The complete name of the study must be included in the first sentence. The study acronym should not be included in this section. Study Acronym This section should include the study acronym, which may not necessarily be derived from the initials of the study title. For example, the acronym RALES stands for Randomized ALdactone Evaluation Study for congestive heart failure. The full title of this study was The effect of spironolactone on morbidity and mortality in patients with severe heart failure. Principal Investigator, Co-investigators, and Collaborating Institutions This section should list the principal investigator, co-investigators, and collaborating institutions involved in the study. Funding sources should not be included in this section. Overview This section provides a general overview of the trial. The study acronym should be mentioned in the first sentence. This overview serves as a summary of all the subsequent sections. Disease State(s) Studied This section should list all the major diseases studied in the trial, including the primary outcome diseases. Study Design This section should describe the study design in detail, including: Setting: Whether the study was conducted at multiple centers or a single center, and if available, the number of sites and countries involved. Type of blinding: Single-blind, double-blind, or open-label (unblinded). Design: The study design type, such as parallel arms (2, 3, or 4), cross-over, factorial, delayed-start, or other. Sample size: The total number of randomized patients, which can be found in the CONSORT flowchart, abstract, or study methods section. Study Duration and Time-points This section should include: Total study duration: Mentioned in the first sentence. Participant enrollment: The total number of years used for participant enrollment, often found with the NCT number in the study abstract. Study start date: The start date of the study, also typically located with the NCT number. Follow-up: The total years of follow-up, including any stoppage criteria and the reasons for stopping, if available. Study visits: The time points at which the primary outcome is assessed. Interventions This section should describe all treatment arms studied in the trial, including both experimental and active comparator (standard treatment) arms. The number of arms should also be specified. Primary Endpoint This section should describe the primary endpoint of the clinical trial. The primary endpoint is the main reason for randomizing subjects and the basis for powering the trial. Composite endpoints (more than two or three primary endpoints) may also be included. Statistical reports should not be included in this section. Secondary Endpoints This section should describe the secondary endpoints of the trial. These are outcomes analyzed post hoc, for which the trial may not be powered or randomized. All secondary endpoints should be listed, but statistical reports should not be included. Inclusion Criteria This section should outline the inclusion criteria, which are the characteristics that prospective subjects must have to be included in the study. Exclusion Criteria This section should outline the exclusion criteria, which are the characteristics that disqualify subjects from being included in the study. Outcome: Primary Endpoint This section should describe the results of the primary endpoint, comparing the experimental and control arms. Statistical reports, including the statistical test used, should be included. The format for reporting results is: XX% vs XX% (RR, HR, OR, SMD; P value; NNT). Outcome: Secondary Endpoint This section should describe the results of the secondary endpoints, comparing the experimental and control arms. Statistical reports, including the statistical test used, should be included. The format for reporting results is: XX% vs XX% (RR, HR, OR, SMD; P value; NNT). Outcome: Exploratory Endpoints This section should describe the results of exploratory endpoints, comparing the experimental and control arms. Statistical reports, including the statistical test used, should be included. Subgroup Analysis This section should describe the results of subgroup analyses, comparing the experimental and control arms. Statistical reports, including the statistical test used, should be included. Outcome: Safety Endpoints This section should describe the results of safety endpoints, comparing the experimental and control arms. Statistical reports, including the statistical test used, should be included. The format for reporting results is: XX% vs XX% (RR, HR, OR, SMD; P value; NNH). Statistical Methods This section should describe the statistical methods used in the trial. It should include: Sample size calculation (if available). Statistical tests used (e.g., T-test, MANCOVA, ANOVA, linear regression, chi-squared, correlation). Level of significance (e.g., X%). Analysis type (e.g., intention-to-treat or per-protocol). Power and effect size (e.g., XX% power to detect a XX% effect with respect to the primary outcome). Conclusions This section should summarize the conclusions of the trial. It should state whether the active intervention is superior, inferior, or equivalent to the control intervention in achieving the primary outcome. The conclusion should also indicate whether the primary endpoint was positive or negative. Discussion and Limitations of the Trial This section should discuss the trial's findings and limitations, addressing potential sources of bias, imprecision, and, if relevant, the multiplicity of analyses. Commentary This section should include personal comments or insights about the study. Slides Slides from the WikiDoc journal club on the trial can be downloaded. Video Commentary This section may include video commentary on the trial. External Sites for Further Information Links to external resources, such as the Wiki Journal Club, may be included for further information.
